---
title: "orbit env:sync"
sidebarTitle: "env:sync"
description: "Replace the Instance's `.env` with the complete stored configuration. Edits to stored keys disappear. The Gateway checks the key names the Node agent reports: a key that exists only in the file stops the sync with `env.sync_would_drop_keys`, unless Orbit wrote or detached that key itself, and a file whose names the agent has not observed stops it with `env.keys_not_observed`. Run `env:import` first (with `--replace` when the file's other keys are already stored), or pass `--force` to replace the file."
---

```bash
orbit env:sync --instance=SELECTOR [--force] [--json]
```

```bash
orbit env:sync --instance=12
```

Both refusals come at admission, before any task starts, and name the keys when the file has them. The agent reads the key names only, never values, and only from a `.env` that Orbit wrote: 0640 with group `orbit-env`. A hand-made 0600 `.env`, a link, a missing file, or a Node whose agent is silent leaves the names not observed. A `.env` written before Orbit used this mode is 0600 too. For such a file, run `env:import`, then `env:sync --force`: the import stores the file's keys, so the forced sync drops none and writes the file as 0640. `--force` alone replaces the file; the keys only it held are gone.

The Gateway answers at once with the started Operation. The CLI follows it until it ends and prints the outcome, the failed step and error code if any, the Operation ID, and the request ID. With `--json`, it prints only the final Operation, whose `result` holds the [synchronization result](/reference/environment-variables#operations). The command exits nonzero unless the Operation succeeds. Ctrl-C stops following; the Operation keeps running, and `orbit operation:show ID` shows it.

<Note>
On production Instances, every sync refreshes the selected PHP runtime without a deploy, even when `.env` is unchanged. If the current release has `bootstrap/cache/config.php`, Orbit runs `php artisan config:cache` there as the Instance user, then reloads PHP-FPM to reset its opcache. An uncached release stays uncached. The Operation result reports `refreshed`, or `skipped_no_php_version` when no PHP version is selected. Development Instances keep the file-only behavior, and their result reports `skipped_development`.

After the reload, Orbit restarts running Instance Processes that have `restart_on_deploy` enabled and reports their IDs. A failed cache build, reload or restart fails the Operation with `env.runtime_refresh_failed`. Fix the reported problem and repeat `env:sync`. Deploys and Route-domain transitions do not run this env-sync refresh.
</Note>

When the end check `Check the written file` fails, the file on the Node differs from the rendering. Run the command again: it writes the file again.

## On a container Instance

On an Instance in a container, `env:sync` does not render the whole file, unlike on a host Instance. Orbit never renders an existing container's `.env` again. The sync writes ONLY the keys of the Instance's attached connections and the keys that `env:update` stored since the last sync, in place, in the `.env` inside the container: for a MySQL or PostgreSQL connection under prefix `DB`, `DB_CONNECTION`, `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME` and `DB_PASSWORD`. Run it after `database:create --instance`, `instance:database:add` or `env:update` on an existing container Instance. `--force` has no effect there, and `env:import` stays refused for a container.

A key that `env:update` stores on a container Instance waits for the next `env:sync`. That sync writes it once, with the stored value, by the rules below. A connection key of the same name keeps the connection's line. After a passed sync the key leaves the wait list: later syncs do not write it again, so a later hand edit of that line stays. A failed sync keeps the wait list. A key whose stored value is gone, for example after a detach, leaves the list unwritten. `env:update` on a container is refused with `instance.lifecycle_busy` while a sync of it runs, because that sync clears the keys it admitted. A pending key is rendered as a full render renders it: a `{{instance.domain}}` value needs the Instance's one settled Route, else the sync is refused with `env.reference_unavailable` or `env.owner_unavailable`. Store the key again with a plain value to go on.

- A key the file already has gets the connection's value, also when the owner set it by hand.
- A key the file lacks is added at the end.
- A key whose value holds a `${...}` reference stays as the Project wrote it. The result names it under `kept`.
- Every other line stays byte for byte, and the file keeps its owner, group, mode and ACL.

The keys include the seven keys of an attached [websocket app](/reference/websocket-apps#reach-from-a-container). The same Operation, `instance.connection_environment`, first adds the container's network paths to each attached server: the ACL egress rule, the bridge endpoint and the UFW rule. It removes no database rule. The path to a websocket app's private endpoint is reconciled: the run keeps only the ACL rule and UFW rule its plan names, and writes the plan's [private names](/reference/development-containers#private-names-of-the-access-plan) into the container's `/etc/hosts`. After a remove, the next sync withdraws them; the keys stay in the file. A clone's [own site](/reference/development-containers#the-own-site-from-inside) rules, `Orbit own site` and `Orbit own development ports`, are reconciled the same way, by their descriptions. When the file changed, it clears Laravel's configuration cache and restarts the Instance's own running units: its FrankenPHP unit and its running Process units. The values reach the container only through a Swamp vault copy; the Operation input and result hold key names only. The result lists the key names under `written`, `added`, `kept` and `unchanged`, and the restarted units under `restarted`.

With no key to write, the sync still runs, so it can withdraw a removed app's path. The sync is refused, and no run starts, when the container is stopped (`process.target_inactive`), or when lifecycle work is unfinished (`instance.lifecycle_busy`). A `.env` that is missing, a link, or holds a quoted value that never closes fails the run with `env.configuration_invalid`; the file stays as it was. The run fails with `env.connection_changed` when the attached connections, or the stored keys it is to write, changed after admission; run `env:sync` again. Another failed step ends as `instance.connection_environment_failed`.
